page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-192-lssd is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 192 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor with 96 physical cores and a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The processor includes 504 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. The system is equipped with 720 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core. For local storage, it bundles 32 NVMe SSDs totaling 12,599 GB of high-speed storage. No GPUs are included.

Benchmark results place this server in the top tier (top 10%) for multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 208,109.69 and a PassMark CPU score of 154,353.09. It exhibits strong memory bandwidth, achieving 15,326.29 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 711.18 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Database and web serving capabilities are also in the top tier, as demonstrated by 329.28 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 173.18 GB/sec.

While multi-core and parallel tasks excel, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the average (middle 50%) tier. For large language model (LLM) inference, the server shows a clear performance tradeoff: prompt processing speeds are strong (top 25%) across 135M, 7B, and 70B models, but text generation speeds drop to the average tier (middle 50%) for the 135M and 70B models.

Given its high resource density, including 192 dedicated vCPUs and over 12 TB of local NVMe SSD storage, this instance offers high qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring massive parallel processing and high-throughput local storage. It is highly suited for large-scale database operations, software compilation, data-intensive web serving, and multi-threaded decompression tasks.
